cards.text: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ (James 1:1), is writing to believers he calls his brothers. He's just finished warning rich people who held back the wages of their workers (James 5:4). Now he turns back to the brothers and tells them to be patient until the Lord's coming.

cards.question: James wants to give the brothers a picture of patience they can see. Who does he point to?
The farmer in James's picture is waiting on the precious fruit of the soil. What is he patient for?

cards.text: Then James turns it right back to the brothers: you, too, be patient. That farmer can't hurry the rain any more than I can hurry my oven timer, and friend, I have BEGGED that timer.

cards.question: James tells the brothers that they, too, should be patient and strengthen their hearts. Why?

answers.text: Their hard work will pay off

cards.text: Near, James says. He doesn't give a date, and Jesus said only the Father knows the day (Matthew 24:36), so my job is simple: keep the ovens ready.
Next, James has a warning about how the brothers treat one another.

cards.question: While the brothers wait, what does James tell them not to do to one another?
James tells the brothers not to complain about each other, so they won't be judged. Then he tells them to look, because the ___ is standing at the door.

cards.text: Picture griping about a coworker, then looking up, and the boss is standing RIGHT there in the doorway. Now make it the Judge, and watch how fast my mustache covers my mouth.
Then James gives the brothers some people to look at. He calls them an example of patience in affliction.

cards.question: Who does James give the brothers as an example of patience in affliction?

answers.text: The prophets who spoke in the Lord's name
The kings who ruled over all Israel
The priests who served in the temple

cards.text: James says we consider those who have persevered blessed. Then he names one man the brothers have heard about, a man who lost his flocks, his herds and his children (Job 1:13-19).

cards.question: Which man's perseverance does James remind the brothers about?

cards.text: James reminds them they've seen the outcome the Lord brought for Job. Honestly, I did years in a junk drawer and thought I had it rough, but Job makes my drawer look like a vacation.

cards.question: After bringing up Job, what does James say about the Lord?

answers.text: He is full of compassion and mercy
He rewards those who wait for Him
He tests those who love Him

cards.text: Then James says, "Above all, my brothers," and turns to the way they talk.

cards.question: James says not by heaven, not by earth, not by anything else. What does he tell the brothers not to do?
True or false: James says a plain yes or no is enough, so they won't fall under judgment.

cards.text: Next, James goes mood by mood. Is anyone suffering? He should pray.

cards.question: And if one of the brothers is cheerful, what does James say he should do?

cards.text: Next on James's list: anyone who's sick.

cards.question: Who does James say a sick person should call?
True or false: James says the elders should pray over the sick person and anoint him with oil in the name of the Lord.
What does James say the prayer offered in faith will do for the one who is sick?

answers.text: It will show him his sin

cards.question: James says the Lord will raise the sick one up. And if he has sinned, he will be ___.

cards.text: So James tells the brothers to confess their sins to each other and pray for each other, so that they may be healed.

cards.question: What does James say the prayer of a righteous man has?

cards.text: Then James brings up Elijah, a prophet in Israel (1 Kings 18:36). And he points out that Elijah was a man just like us.

cards.question: What did Elijah pray earnestly for?

answers.text: That the sun would stand still

cards.question: After Elijah prayed, how long did it not rain on the land?
Then Elijah prays again. James says the heavens give ___, and the earth yields its ___.

cards.text: James has one more thing for the brothers. What if one of them wanders from the truth, and someone brings him back?

cards.question: James says whoever turns a sinner from the error of his way will do what?

answers.text: Earn a place among the elders

cards.text: And he'll cover over a multitude of sins. That's where James ends his whole letter, friend, with one brother bringing another one back.

findings.problem: This story card adds nothing new from the passage. It goes back over James 5:8, which card 5 already answered, to make a side point about Matthew 24:36. The walkthrough doesn't move forward on this card. The Matthew 24:36 line could ride along on card 7, which does move forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke about James 5:9, which cards 8 and 9 already covered. It tells no new part of the passage. The joke should ride along on a card that tells part of the passage, such as card 11.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'He rewards those who wait for Him' is close to what James 5:11 says: those who persevere are blessed, and Job saw the outcome from the Lord. Card 15 has just told the baker about 'the outcome the Lord brought for Job.' A baker could argue that this wrong answer is right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop. 8 of its 10 choice cards are multiple choice, with only 1 true or false card and 1 fill in the blank card.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop. 7 of its 10 choice cards are multiple choice, with only 1 true or false card and 2 fill in the blank cards.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: No card in stop 2 has a joke, a reaction or any of Papa Dorin's personality. The story cards are flat summaries ('Next on James's list: anyone who's sick.'). Moments like Elijah being 'a man just like us' or the three and a half years without rain could hold a real laugh without muddying a fact.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The story card before this question (card 10) only says that Elijah was a prophet and a man just like us. It gives nothing about rain or drought that the baker could use to reason toward 'That it would not rain' over the other answers. The only way to pick is luck or knowing the story already. The setup should give more context.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.
